name: Sync orders and stock across Shopify, WooCommerce and marketplaces with Google Sheets and WhatsApp reports

parameters.content:
## Sync orders and stock across Shopify, WooCommerce and marketplaces with Google Sheets and WhatsApp reports

### How it works
1. New orders arrive from Shopify, WooCommerce and a secured webhook for marketplaces, POS or aggregators.
2. Each order is normalized, checked for SKUs, logged once in the Orders tab and written to a stock ledger.
3. Current stock (start stock plus every movement) is pushed back to Shopify and WooCommerce, so all shops show the same quantity.
4. When a SKU drops to its alert level you get an email and a WhatsApp message.
5. Every evening a sales report goes out by email and as a WhatsApp summary.

### Setup steps
- [ ] Add **Shopify** (access token), **WooCommerce**, **Header Auth**, **Google Sheets**, **Gmail** and **WhatsApp** credentials.
- [ ] Create the Data Table `hub_stock_moves` (sku, qty, order_key, channel, created_at, all *String*).
- [ ] Create a spreadsheet with an `Inventory` tab (SKU, Name, Start Stock, Counted At, Low Stock At, Shopify Inventory Item ID, WooCommerce Product ID) and empty `Orders` and `Error Log` tabs. Select it in every Google Sheets node.
- [ ] Get two WhatsApp templates approved and edit **Hub Settings** and **Report Settings**.

### Customization
After a stock count, update Start Stock and Counted At.

## Receive orders from every channel
Shopify, WooCommerce and a webhook for marketplaces.

## Log each order once
Repeated webhooks are skipped.

## Update the stock ledger
One movement per order line.

## Sync stock to the shops
Sets the new quantity everywhere.

## Alert on low stock
Email and WhatsApp when a SKU crosses its level.

## Build the daily report
Sales, best sellers and low stock.

## Send the report
Email first, then a WhatsApp summary.

## Catch workflow errors
Builds an incident report from any failed execution.

## Send the alert
Emails it, or logs it to the Error Log tab.

nodes.name: Shopify Order
nodes.notes: Registers an orders/create webhook in your store and checks every call against the app secret.

nodes.name: WooCommerce Order
nodes.notes: Registers an order.created webhook in WooCommerce and checks its signature.

nodes.name: Marketplace Order
nodes.notes: For Tokopedia, Shopee, TikTok Shop or a POS through an aggregator or Make/Zapier. JSON: {"channel","order_id","created_at","customer_name","customer_phone","currency","total","items":[{"sku","name","quantity","price"}]}.

nodes.name: Hub Settings
nodes.notes: EDIT ME. low_stock_template is "template_name|language" of an approved WhatsApp template with one body variable. shopify_shop is the part before .myshopify.com.

nodes.name: Normalize Order
nodes.notes: Every line needs a SKU: it is the key that links the channels to your Inventory tab.

parameters.errorMessage: ={{ '[WARNING] ' + $json.channel + ' order ' + ($json.order_id || '(no id)') + ' was not processed: ' + $json.problems.join('; ') + '. Fix the product SKUs in that channel, then enter the sale manually.' }}

nodes.name: Escalate · Invalid Order
nodes.notes: The built-in error handler emails this. Stock is not touched for invalid orders.

nodes.name: Skip Repeat Orders
nodes.notes: Shops resend webhooks after timeouts. An order key already handled is never counted twice.

nodes.name: Build Order Row
nodes.notes: Field names = Orders sheet headers.

nodes.name: Log Order
nodes.notes: All channels in one tab: the dashboard for daily sales. Minimise API Calls is on, so the Sheets append API adds the row and two orders at the same moment never overwrite each other.

nodes.name: One Item per Line
nodes.notes: Each order line becomes one item under "line", next to the order key and channel.

nodes.name: Record Stock Move
nodes.notes: An append-only stock ledger: two orders at the same moment can never overwrite each other's stock change.

nodes.name: Get SKU Moves
nodes.notes: Every movement of the SKUs in this order.

nodes.name: Read Inventory
nodes.notes: Your master stock list: SKU, Name, Start Stock, Counted At, Low Stock At, Shopify Inventory Item ID, WooCommerce Product ID.

nodes.name: Compute Stock
nodes.notes: One item per SKU of the order. crossed_low is true only on the order that pushes the stock to or below Low Stock At, so you get one alert, not one per order.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ location_id: Number($('Hub Settings').first().json.shopify_location_id), inventory_item_id: Number($json.shopify_item_id), available: Math.max(0, $json.current) }) }}

nodes.name: Set Shopify Stock
nodes.notes: Sets the absolute quantity, so repeating it is harmless. Negative hub stock is sent as 0.

nodes.name: Set WooCommerce Stock
nodes.notes: Simple products. For variations, switch the resource to Product Variation.

nodes.name: Crossed Low Stock?
nodes.notes: Also lets unknown SKUs through, so a missing Inventory row is noticed.

parameters.subject: ={{ 'Stock alert · ' + $('Crossed Low Stock?').all().map(i => i.json.sku).join(', ') }}

parameter.text: ={{ $('Crossed Low Stock?').all().filter(i => i.json.known).map(i => i.json.sku + ' ' + i.json.name + ': ' + i.json.current).join('; ').slice(0, 900) || 'unknown SKU, see email' }}

nodes.name: WhatsApp Stock Alert
nodes.notes: A WhatsApp template message, so it also reaches you outside the 24-hour window. Template body example: "Stok menipis: {{1}}".

nodes.name: Every Day at 21:00
nodes.notes: Uses the workflow time zone.

nodes.name: Report Settings
nodes.notes: EDIT ME. report_template: an approved WhatsApp template with five body variables (date, revenue, orders, best seller, low stock).

nodes.name: Build Daily Report
nodes.notes: Totals are in the report currency; orders in another currency are counted as they are.

parameters.subject: ={{ 'Sales ' + $json.date + ': ' + $json.revenue_text + ' from ' + $json.orders + ' orders' }}

nodes.name: WhatsApp Daily Report
nodes.notes: Template body example: "Laporan {{1}}: omzet {{2}} dari {{3}} pesanan. Terlaris: {{4}}. Stok menipis: {{5}}." Sent after the email, so a template problem never blocks the email.

nodes.name: On Workflow Error
nodes.notes: Internal error workflow: n8n starts here when any production execution of THIS workflow fails (and Settings → Error workflow is empty).

nodes.name: Alert Settings
nodes.notes: EDIT ME. Who gets incident alerts. Comma-separate multiple emails.

assignments.name: severity
error_message
assignments.value: ={{ String($('On Workflow Error').first().json.execution?.error?.message ?? $('On Workflow Error').first().json.trigger?.error?.message ?? 'No error message provided').slice(0, 2000) }}

nodes.name: Build Incident Report
nodes.notes: Normalises the Error Trigger payload (execution errors and trigger errors have different shapes) into one incident record.

Next step: open the failed execution, check the input of the failed node, fix the cause, then use Retry → From failed node in the Executions list.

nodes.name: Email Alert
nodes.notes: Primary alert. Email is independent of the services this workflow calls, so their outage cannot silence the alert. Retries 3× / 5 s, then the fallback runs.

nodes.name: Error Log Row
nodes.notes: Shapes the Error Log columns and renames the email failure reason. Keeps a field called 'error' away from the Sheets node: Retry On Fail treats an output item with 'error' as a failed try and would append the row again.

nodes.name: Fallback · Log to Error Sheet
nodes.notes: Only runs when the email alert failed after 3 tries. Appends the incident to the 'Error Log' tab; the header row is created on first use. If this fails too, the error run shows as failed in Executions.
